videos.script: A prompt for a programming task is a ticket. It works when a colleague could do the job from it without coming back to ask. {{ticket}} In this lesson the shop learns to read a price typed with a comma. First with one line, and an answer that breaks the project's rules. Then with a goal, context, constraints, a definition of done, and a format. {{anatomy}} You paste the evidence instead of describing it, and ask for a diff that git can check before anything changes. {{diff}} You split the task into a plan, tests and a change, and feed the failing test back when the change is not enough. {{loop}} At the end, the prompt becomes code. It lives in the repository, it has tests, and two versions of it are compared with numbers instead of impressions. {{eval}}
